title: The flash-sale checkout that never hits 25% off
topic: A holiday discount the AI 'finished' in one sitting
blurb: Spec says $500+ gets 25% off. The AI's function is very sure it does. Big carts will disagree.
prompt: Spec: sum every item, take 25% off at $500+ or 10% off at $100+, return the total. An AI intern shipped this for the flash sale. Review it.

segments.label: L2
segments.text: subtotal = sum(prices[i] for i in range(len(prices) - 1))

conclusion: AI summary: Sums all prices and applies 10% off at $100+ or 25% off at $500+. Ready for the sale.

flaws.corrupted: subtotal = sum(prices[i] for i in range(len(prices) - 1))

diagnosis_choices.label: `range(len(prices) - 1)` stops one short, silently dropping the last item.
`range(len(prices) - 1)` raises IndexError whenever `prices` has only one item.
Python's `sum()` requires a list `[...]`, so passing a generator returns `0`.
`range` starts at index `1`, so `prices[0]` is skipped on every cart.

fix_choices.label: Use `range(1, len(prices))` so the loop reaches the final item's index.
Wrap the generator in brackets `[prices[i] for i in range(len(prices) - 1)]`.

flaws.explanation: `range(n)` generates `0 .. n-1`. Subtracting 1 cuts off the final element of `prices` (and gives 0 for a single-item cart!).
flaws.why_tempting: People remember 'last index is `len - 1`' and forget that `range()` already excludes its stop value.
flaws.catch_rule: Test loops on a 1-element list: if `range(len(xs) - 1)` runs 0 times, it's off by one.
flaws.hint: What's `subtotal` when the cart is just `prices = [200]`?

practice.problem: For `xs = [10, 20, 30]`, which values does `xs[i]` hit when `i` runs through `range(len(xs) - 1)`?
practice.answer: Only `10` and `20`. The last item, `30`, never gets added.

flaws.original: if subtotal >= 500: discount = 0.25  # check the higher threshold first

diagnosis_choices.label: Dead branch: every `subtotal >= 500` already hit `if subtotal >= 100` on L3.
Python forbids checking the same variable `subtotal` in both `if` and `elif`.
Using `>= 500` instead of `> 500` gives $500 orders 25% off when they only get 10%.
An `elif` branch runs *after* `if` too, stacking 10% and 25% into 35% off.

fix_choices.label: Check the higher tier first: `if subtotal >= 500:` (0.25), then `elif subtotal >= 100:` (0.10).
Change `elif subtotal >= 500:` to `if subtotal >= 500:` while keeping L3 at `>= 100` — wait, keep `elif subtotal < 500:`.
Remove the `else:` branch on L7 so Python evaluates both thresholds independently.
Swap `0.10` on L4 and `0.25` on L6 without changing the threshold order.

flaws.explanation: In an `if / elif` chain, only the first true branch runs. Because every number `>= 500` is also `>= 100`, the 25% tier is dead code.
flaws.why_tempting: Listing tiers from smallest ($100) to largest ($500) reads naturally in English, even though `if/elif` requires the reverse.
flaws.catch_rule: In threshold `if/elif` chains, always order conditions from most restrictive to least restrictive (highest to lowest for `>=`).
flaws.hint: Walk a $600 order through lines 3–6. Which branch actually runs?

practice.problem: In `if score >= 60: g='D' elif score >= 90: g='A'`, what grade does 95 get?

clean_conclusion: Every item is summed, and a $500+ cart actually gets the 25% tier.

diagnosis: If `prices` is empty `[]`, `checkout_total` crashes with ValueError without an early guard.
Missing default `prices=[]` prevents calling `checkout_total` on empty carts.
Accepting floats in `prices` breaks `>= 100` comparisons without `Decimal`.
Function mutates `prices` in place during `sum(...)`.
fix: Add `if not prices: return 0.0` right after line 1.
Default `prices = []` in the signature.
Convert all entries with `map(int, prices)` on line 1.
Clone `prices = list(prices)` before summing.

diagnosis: Using `>= 100` gives 10% off at exactly `$100` when the spec requires strictly over `$100`.
`if subtotal >= 100:` skips `$500+` carts only if L5 runs before L3 — here L3 itself should check `subtotal < 500` too.
Comparing float `subtotal >= 100` fails when `subtotal` is `100.0`.
The first tier should check `subtotal > 0` before checking `100`.
fix: Change `>= 100` to `> 100` so `$100` exact stays full price.
Add an upper bound: `if 100 <= subtotal < 500:` on line 3.
Compare against `100.0` instead of integer `100`.
Check `if subtotal < 100: discount = 0.0` first.

diagnosis: Setting `discount = 0.10` takes 90% off instead of 10% off when multiplied on L8.
Discount should be `10` (percentage points), not `0.10`.
`discount` is scoped inside the `if` block and becomes undefined on L8.
Assigning `0.10` here is overwritten by L7 `else` on every call.
fix: Set `discount = 0.90` so L8 keeps 90% of the subtotal.
Initialize `discount = 0.0` above L3 so it stays in scope.
Set `discount = 10` and divide by `100` on L8.
Return `round(subtotal * 0.9, 2)` directly on L4.

diagnosis: Setting `discount = 0.25` charges only 25% of the cart instead of taking 25% off.
25% off on top of 10% off should be `discount = 0.15` so they don't stack to 35%.
Floating-point `0.25` introduces binary rounding error; use `1 / 4` instead.
`discount` isn't returned here, so execution falls through to `else: discount = 0.0`.
fix: Change `discount = 0.25` to `discount = 0.75`.
Change to `discount = 0.15` so total discount caps at 25%.
Add `return` right after `discount = 0.25` so it doesn't fall into `else`.
Use `discount = 25` and divide by 100 on line 8.

diagnosis: Putting `discount = 0.0` on the same line after `else:` is a syntax error in Python.
This `else:` only pairs with `elif` on L5, so carts between `$100` and `$499` get reset to `0.0`.
Setting `discount = 0.0` makes L8 multiply by `0` and return `$0` for small carts.
Missing `return` on `else:` causes small carts to return `None`.
fix: Put `discount = 0.0` on the next indented line under `else:`.
Initialize `discount = 0.0` before L3 and remove the `else:` branch.
Set `discount = 1.0` on `else:` so small carts pay 100%.
Return `round(subtotal, 2)` directly in the `else:` branch.

diagnosis: Formula is inverted: `subtotal * (1 - discount)` charges 10% instead of taking 10% off.
Should be `subtotal * discount` to compute the discounted total.
`round(..., 2)` truncates cents downward, undercharging on every `.xx5` cart.
Multiplying `subtotal * (1 - discount)` before checking `subtotal == 0` divides by zero.
fix: Change to `round(subtotal * discount, 2)`.
Change to `round(subtotal / (1 + discount), 2)`.
Use `int(subtotal * (1 - discount))` to avoid float drift.
Subtract `discount` directly: `round(subtotal - discount, 2)`.
